title: Trump, Xi and Putin Speak at APEC Plenary in Shenzhen Before First Trilateral
excerpt: Xi Jinping opened the Shenzhen plenary with a $20 million cooperation pledge as the three presidents prepared for the first-ever US-China-Russia leaders' meeting, with Iran, nuclear arms and a fragile trade truce in the background.
body:
• Xi Jinping opened the APEC leaders' plenary in Shenzhen on Thursday, pledging $20 million for Asia-Pacific cooperation in digital technology and clean energy, with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in the room.
  • Trump cast the United States as a Pacific power and warned against regulation that would "stifle" artificial intelligence; Putin called Russia an "integral part" of the Asia-Pacific and invited partners to use Russian logistics infrastructure.
  • The three presidents were due to meet face to face later on Thursday at Shenzhen's Kylin Villa, in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia.
  • Expectations are low: the White House does not expect a formal agreement, and the US-China trade truce that forms the meeting's backdrop expires on January 10, 2027.

The leaders of the world's three most powerful militaries took their seats in Shenzhen on Thursday morning for the opening plenary of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, hours before a three-way meeting that has no precedent. The plenary began just before 10:00 a.m. local time at the Shenzhen International Exchange Center, with the leaders posing for a group photograph before host Xi Jinping opened the session, Aju Press and Nikkei Asia reported.

Xi used his opening address to cast China as the defender of an open Asia-Pacific. He proposed four pillars for regional development — economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development — and said China would provide $20 million for work on digital technology and clean energy, Nikkei Asia reported. "China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation," he said, according to the BBC's live coverage.

Trump followed with a defence of American power in the region and a promise not to restrain the artificial-intelligence industry. "The United States has been a Pacific power for hundreds of years, and we continue to work to promote growth and stability, sovereignty, prosperity and peace throughout this region," he said, according to Nikkei Asia. He described AI as "almost completely good" and said regulation must not be allowed to "stifle" the sector, the BBC reported. Putin, speaking after Xi, said Russia was an "integral part" of the Asia-Pacific, invited partners to use Russian logistics infrastructure, and said "economic domination and coercion are now a thing of the past," Nikkei Asia and the BBC reported.

The meeting still to come

The plenary was the overture. Trump and Xi were scheduled to meet first on Thursday at 12:45 p.m. Shenzhen time — their third bilateral meeting of the year — before Putin joined them for three-way talks at the Kylin Villa, a state-owned compound in Shenzhen, Aju Press reported. The trilateral is expected to last roughly an hour. It is the first formal three-way meeting between the presidents of the United States, China and Russia, held on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, which China is hosting in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19.

The choreography began on Wednesday, when Xi personally greeted Trump at Shenzhen airport and the three men appeared together at a welcome banquet, flanking their host for the group photograph.

What Washington wants on the table

The White House has said Trump plans to discuss the war with Iran as well as a possible three-way agreement on nuclear armament, according to Al Jazeera's explainer on the meeting. Ukraine is not expected to be on the formal agenda, as Xi is understood to be reluctant to be drawn into what he views as a European matter. On nuclear arms, the New START treaty between Russia and the United States lapsed in February; Trump previously rejected Russia's proposal to extend it, demanding instead a new deal that includes Beijing, while Xi is understood to be unenthusiastic about joining a treaty China had no part in writing, Al Jazeera reported.

"It's a summit of Trump's ego, Putin's tactics, China's strategy."

— Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin, to Al Jazeera

The trade truce clock

The economic file is just as consequential. At the height of the tariff war, US tariffs on Chinese goods reached 145 percent and China retaliated with 125 percent, before a temporary truce agreed in Busan, South Korea, in October 2025. The truce has since been extended to January 10, 2027, but China's rare-earth exports to the United States remain about 75 percent below normal levels, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies, cited by Al Jazeera. Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation, told Al Jazeera that a handshake without incident would be seen as a win.

Why Putin's presence is itself the story

For Putin, the value is largely symbolic: standing as an equal alongside the leaders of the world's two largest economies challenges years of Western efforts to isolate him over Ukraine. "For Putin, this meeting holds primarily symbolic significance, illustrating the decline of American dominance by establishing a precedent for this trilateral format," Oleg Ignatov, senior Russia analyst at Crisis Group, told Le Monde. The Kremlin has denied any intent to carve up the world: "To say that someone or other intends to decide the fate of the world, this is not Russia, definitely not China," a Russian government spokesperson said on November 16, Le Monde reported.

What to watch

The trilateral may produce a short statement, a commitment to keep talking, or nothing at all. The White House does not expect a formal agreement, which makes the meeting itself the main political fact. What it settles on Iran, nuclear arms and the trade truce becomes clear only after the Kylin Villa session ends.
